purpose: Synchronized Oracle instruction-count ablation of only R114 borrowed input dispatch versus correct R113; physical router collection remains the performance authority.
sampling: Two same-ELF R113 A/A pairs then two reversed-order pairs at each of 0/64 held clients. Fixed12 samples, fresh normalized-length daemon launch each time; no optional extension.
analysis: Descriptive paired counts per validated send, report every raw sample and A/A spread. No IID confidence claim for the balanced permutation cycle, no equivalence test or acceptance based on Oracle CPU.
decision: Describe instructions, branches, misses, cycles and clocks. This can locate eliminated user-mode work; it cannot show router CPU superiority or remove the C comparison gaps. No causal compiler-layout claim or acceptance from these counters.
boundaries: Enable ACK after warmup before the three clock reads; disable ACK after the loop and the three clock reads. No per-request instrumentation. Final callback validates delivery; bounded trailing daemon work can straddle the CPU-clock/disable boundary. Counts include this boundary overhead and are divided by 50000.
limitations: Unique temporary path content still varies, but path byte lengths, basename and socket argument byte lengths are identical for every subject.
The pathname dependence mechanism has not been proven to be allocator placement.
The chosen diagnostic launch name is not a deployment measurement. Router runs still decide performance.
